title: Eval Harness: Prompt Set Catalog & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Asha Kumar
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the canonical prompt-set catalog schema for Redwood's eval harness, the responsibilities and procedures for prompt-set onboarding, how prompt sets and benchmarks are used in automated regression detection, and the triage/escalation flow when quality regressions are detected. It also documents how quantization profiles and model variants are integrated into the eval pipeline and provides reproducible examples and CLI snippets for common workflows.

Scope:
- Applies to all prompt sets and benchmarks used by the applied-ml, model-onboarding, and eval-harness teams.
- Covers onboarding, labeling/metadata, automated daily/weekly runs, regression alerting thresholds, first-line triage, and escalation to model owners.
- Excludes ad-hoc local prompt experiments; these should be promoted to the catalog to be covered by this playbook.

Owners and Contacts:
- Primary owner: Applied ML Evals (engineering)
- On-call for eval infra: eng-sre-evals@redwood.ai
- Model onboarding contact: model-onboarding@redwood.ai
- Pager escalation: see related incident playbooks (link in related_pages)

Prompt Set Catalog: Purpose and Principles
- Single source of truth: The catalog stores approved prompt sets used for continuous regression detection and benchmark comparisons.
- Reproducibility: Each prompt set entry must include versioned data, seed/ RNG notes, and an input/output normalization spec.
- Minimal but rich metadata: Schema balances machine-readability (for CI/automation) and human context (for triage).

Catalog schema (fields) - human-readable table (each entry is a YAML/JSON document in the catalog store):
- id: short unique slug (e.g. "summarize-news-2026-q1")
- title: human-friendly title
- description: short description and intended use-case
- domain_tags: list (e.g., ["summarization", "news"])
- created_by: author name/email
- version: semantic version (e.g., "v1.2")
- provenance: source (internal/synthetic/third-party) and source_link if applicable
- examples_count: integer (number of prompt-example pairs)
- positive_criteria: short description of success conditions (for automated pass/fail)
- negative_criteria: known failure modes to label as high-severity
- normalization: tokenization/whitespace/temperature seeds used for eval runs
- labels_schema: list of annotation fields and allowed values
- required_metrics: list (e.g., ["rouge-l", "exact_match", "toxicity_score"])
- schedule: cron-like string for automated runs (e.g., "0 3 * * *")
- owner_team: team slug responsible for triage
- contact: email or slack handle
- confidentiality: internal|restricted

Sample prompt-set metadata (YAML):
---
id: summarize-news-2026-q1
title: News summarization - cross-source
description: Short summaries for current-events articles across multiple publishers
domain_tags: ["summarization", "news"]
created_by: asha.kumar@redwood.ai
version: v1.0
provenance: internal
examples_count: 1200
positive_criteria: summary captures main facts and key numeric details; abstractive style allowed
negative_criteria: hallucinated facts, invented numbers, privacy leakage
normalization: { tokenization: bpe, strip_html: true }
labels_schema: [ { name: "faithfulness", values: ["pass", "partial", "fail"] }, { name: "safety", values: ["ok", "flag"] } ]
required_metrics: ["rouge-l", "faithfulness_score"]
schedule: "0 3 * * *"
owner_team: applied-ml
contact: #applied-ml-evals
confidentiality: internal
---

Prompt tagging and labelling guidance:
- Use domain_tags to enable quick filtering (topic, format, style).
- Maintain at most 8 tags per prompt set.
- labels_schema must be precise: include definitions and examples for each label value.
- For human annotations, attach annotation instructions and an example of edge-case judgments.

Automated regression detection: metrics, baselines, and thresholds
- Baseline window: 14-day rolling median is used as the canonical baseline for automated alerts unless a longer window is explicitly requested by the owner_team.
- Detection algorithm: One-sided z-score with bootstrapped confidence; alert if metric drops/increases beyond 3-sigma relative to baseline and p<0.01.
- Minimum sample threshold: only run alerting if examples_count >= 100 and at least 30 new responses are observed in the window.
- Tiered threshold policy (default):
  - P0 alert (immediate page): drop in primary metric >= 10% absolute AND failure-rate increase >= 3x.
  - P1 alert (email + slack): drop >= 5% or new failing safety flags in >1% of responses.
  - P2 alert (report): smaller drifts that are statistically significant but below operational impact thresholds.

Example thresholds table (text):
- primary_metric: rouge-l; baseline: 0.42; P1 threshold: 0.40; P0 threshold: 0.38
- safety_toxicity: baseline: 0.0015; P1 threshold: 0.003; P0 threshold: 0.01

Regression triage workflow (step-by-step)
1. Alert received in #eval-alerts Slack with autogenerated summary: prompt_set id, metric, baseline, current value, top failing examples, and suggested suspect changes (model version, quantization profile, routing change).
2. First-responder (Applied ML oncall): validate alert by re-running the eval-harness locally against the last 500 examples and checking run logs for pipeline errors (3 steps, should take <30 minutes).
3. Quick attribution checklist (ordered):
   a. Check model version/variant changes in last-deploy window.
   b. Check quantization profile changes applied to the serving variant.
   c. Check routing/fallback policies (e.g., traffic shifted to cheaper variant).
   d. Verify eval infra and tokenization/versioning mismatches.
4. If attribution is found (model change, quantization, config drift), attach evidence and assign to owner_team with severity label.
5. If no attribution, escalate to the model owner and schedule a joint investigation (within 4 business hours for P0/P1).
6. Mitigation options: rollback to prior model, pin traffic to stable variant, or apply temporary post-processing filters (safety) while investigation proceeds.
7. Postmortem & follow-up: add incident summary to the regression-triage tracker and update prompt set metadata / required_metrics if needed.

Triage playbook checklist (for first-responder):
- Reproduce the regression locally and snapshot outputs.
- Confirm metric calc code hasn't changed (compare artifact sha).
- Confirm input normalization/versioning is identical between baseline and current runs.
- Re-run a subset with and without quantization to spot quality delta attributable to quantization.
- If quantization implicated, record the profile id and quantization tool logs.

Quantization profiles: integration into eval pipeline
- Each quantization profile is registered in the eval catalog with fields: profile_id, base_model, hardware_target, quant_bits, known_issues, expected_quality_delta (per metric), created_by, created_at.
- During automated runs, the eval-harness executes the same prompt set across the canonical set of model variants + quantization profiles declared in the prompt-set entry.
- Recommended guardrail: if expected_quality_delta > 3% on a required_metric, mark profile as "requires-manual-review" and do not auto-promote to serving.

Model onboarding checklist (minimum for promoting a model to production-ready in Redwood):
1. Unit tests: tokenization / tokenizer alignment tests pass.
2. Eval-harness runs: pass all required prompt sets with no P0/P1 alerts in 30-day trial window.
3. Quantization regression test: run all supported quantization profiles; document quality deltas.
4. Performance validation: latency & throughput targets met on representative hardware.
5. Security & privacy scan: no known unsafe completions in safety-critical prompt sets.
6. Documentation: model card + eval summary + rollout guidance.

Example CLI snippets
- Run eval-harness against a prompt set (local):
redwood-eval run --prompt-set summarize-news-2026-q1 --model rwd-model-3b-v2 --output ./runs/summarize-run.json --limit 500

- Re-run with a quantization profile:
redwood-eval run --prompt-set summarize-news-2026-q1 --model rwd-model-3b-v2 --quant-profile qprofile-int8-rtx6000 --limit 200

Best practices and common pitfalls:
- Always store the seed and normalization pipeline with the prompt set to avoid silent distribution shifts.
- Keep prompt sets small and targeted for fast feedback; large benchmark suites are for periodic evaluation.
- Use measured expected_quality_delta when approving quantization; do not rely on subjective checks alone.
- Document known false-positive triggers for each prompt set to reduce noisy alerts.

Audit and compliance notes:
- All regression alerts and triage artifacts must be retained for 180 days and associated to the model and prompt_set ids for auditability.
- For restricted prompt sets (customer-sensitive), follow the onprem packaging and access controls in eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures.

Appendix: Example automated alert payload (JSON):
{
  "prompt_set_id": "summarize-news-2026-q1",
  "metric": "rouge-l",
  "baseline": 0.421,
  "current": 0.388,
  "delta": -0.033,
  "severity": "P0",
  "top_fail_examples": ["ex1_id","ex45_id","ex221_id"],
  "suspects": ["rwd-model-3b-v2", "qprofile-int8-rtx6000"]
}
